audio_captions: Applause is followed by a woman speaking, "Every morning, we light a candle so that women everywhere know that even until the 11th hour, there's still hope." A clinking sound is heard. The woman continues, "Oops. I believe if we can teach little girls to dream, that they'll be the force that changes this world. But I believe more than that, that if we can teach broken women to dream like little girls again, that would be a force that this world has yet to see. Let me tell you about a little girl halfway across the world, 8,902 miles, not that I count. Mulu."

A woman speaks, "Her name means to be made to be made to be made complete in Afan Oromo. And that is what she did to me." This is followed by a quiet murmur from an audience. She continues, "I wasn't always a candlemaker. I was a nurse, did medical mission trips and fell in love with her. And she completely changed my life and taught me that I could dream. I kept going to her village over and over again and I began to understand..."
A person speaks, "...in the depth of the poverty that was there and I began to understand the issues that they had there. You see..."

A woman speaks, "was just going to see my baby girl. One day, I watched two little girls about five and seven being sold into sex trafficking in the broad daylight, and it shook me in a place that I didn't even know existed. And I knew that somehow we had to become a generation that would go from raped to redeemed. And I knew that task was daunting and I knew that it was going to be impossible to figure out."

A female speaker with a slight echo in her voice says, "But I learned that people need three things to thrive. They need a safe place, they need safe people, and they need a purpose. That was it. We needed to create a purpose. We needed to give them a reason to get out of bed. We needed to give them a reason to not be addicted to drugs. They needed a purpose. We needed to bring light into darkness. What's interesting is that I found myself in these women. I felt their pain and I knew their pain because I too had lived a life of trauma."
A person speaks: "I begin to understand what they needed. I began to see myself in them."
A person speaks, "...and the overwhelming pressures of running a nonprofit and a for-profit, being put on magazine covers..." This is followed by the sound of a soft chime.

A woman speaks, "...speaking in front of thousands, the darkness became so dark that I couldn't see my way out of it. I was supposed to be the light. I was supposed to be the one that told them that they could do this, and I couldn't see my way out of the darkness. And it landed me on a therapist's couch. And I'm gonna let you in on a good secret on how to pick a good therapist. You see, I have crazy wild crazy curly hair. And I picked out the one that had the best curly hair and figured if nothing else, she could teach me how to fix my hair." The audience laughs and applauds. She continues, "Seconds to that, I picked her out based on her quote: Health is a state of complete harmony with the mind, when the body, mind and spirit, when one is free from physical disabilities, mental distractions, the gates of the soul opens."
A character speaks, "Did you catch that when one is free?"
A person says, "She told me about this..." followed by a low musical note.
A person speaks, "It's called EMDR. That if I could briefly relive the trauma and transfer it from one side of my brain to the other,"

A woman speaks, "...that I could be free." A chuckle is heard. She continues, "That if I could withstand going through that, if I could understand what had happened to me and process it from one side to the other, that I could be free. And here's what I learned about..."
A person speaks, "free people. Free people are dangerous people. Free people call truth to BS."

A woman speaks emphatically, "Free people, free people. So don't be chained to the darkness of your past while ushering people to freedom and to light. Don't stand there and wish that you too could find your way to light, because here's the thing about darkness and how you get to light. You have to go through the darkness to get to light. If we turn out all the lights..."

A woman speaks, "in this auditorium and the only thing that was lit was this." This is followed by a clicking sound. The woman continues, "Where light enters, darkness has to flee. It doesn't have a choice. That's just how it works. If that's true, and we feel like our world is dark, then I think we're the answer. What I have learned is what if I had to live through even the darkest of nights to appreciate even the smallest amount of light? What if I had to experience utter darkness so that when somebody was struggling, I could point them to just the the smallest glimmer of light? Just a flicker."
A character speaks in an earnest, clear voice, "We are the antidote to darkness. We are the light that this world so desperately needs. The reason that we..."

A person speaks, "we feel like there's darkness surrounding us is because we've allowed our lights to become dim. And so if you're in a situation and it feels dark, remember that you are the light. And then all it takes is one. And then if the next person lights, and then the next person lights, and then the next person lights, guess what happens? That darkness has to flee. It begins to lead. And men." A piano chord is played.

A woman speaks with a slight echo in her voice, saying, "This topic seems like they're always beating you up. Like you're the bad guys. And the truth is statistically, some of you are. But there's grace and redemption in that. And the truth is that men, you will never see a stronger woman than than a man standing behind her while she speaks her dream. So men, take charge, stand behind the women in your life. Help them speak their dream, help them speak their truth. And you too can speak your dream. You too can be light."
A person speaks in a strained, forceful voice: "So speak your dream. Fight for your freedom. Fight for it like hell," followed by a loud bang as something hits a hard surface.
A woman speaks, "'cause free people, free people. There is a light that shines in the darkness, and the darkness cannot..."
A woman speaks in a deliberate voice, "will not... shall not... overcome it." This is accompanied by a group of people humming in the background.

A man sings solo and is later joined by a choir. They sing, "This little light of mine, I'm gonna let it shine. This little light of mine, I'm gonna let it shine. This little light of mine, I'm gonna let it shine. Let it shine, let it shine, let it shine. Everywhere I go, I'm gonna let it shine. Everywhere I go, I'm gonna let it shine. Everywhere I go, I'm gonna let it shine. Let it shine, let it shine, let it shine. This little light of mine, I'm gonna let it shine. This little light of mine, I'm gonna let it shine. This little light of mine, I'm gonna let it shine. Let it shine, let it shine, let it shine, let it shine, let it shine, let it shine, let it shine." A woman then speaks, "I know that if we can teach little girls to dream, that they'll be the force that changes this world. But I am absolutely certain that if we can teach broken women to dream like little girls again, it'll be a force that this world has yet to see. Thank you." This is followed by loud applause and cheering from a crowd.

audio_captions: A low, distorted voice says, "Hi. Welcome back to Evermind." This is followed by a male voice speaking, "Welcome back to Gigabyte TV, the sciency show where I do stuff with food. I like soda. Now that I've tried it, I like making soda. I put a lot of work into these recipes, so please, try this at home."

Fast-paced electronic music plays, followed by a rattling sound. A person then speaks, "So, the easiest way to make soda is to just take a syrup and then add carbonated water. But that's boring. So, instead, what you can do is take some yeast, add that syrup to it, and then dilute it to your desired volume."

A male voice with a slight echo speaks in a monotone, "Humans would quite likely not be where they are today without yeast. Making alcoholic liquids were the method of creating storable, safe water. Now, that does give us the fruitcake, but that is not the fault of yeast. Besides, yeast also made bread and can produce carbon dioxide, which is going to be used to make our soda pop. If fermented too long, the yeast will produce enough alcohol to make it a hard drink. But the fermentation is stopped early, so only an appreciable amount of carbon dioxide is produced, and there is still sugar left in the drink. Yeast can ferment hexoses and disaccharides, so you can use any natural sweetener from sugar to honey to your own delicious human blood sugar if you can get it."

A person speaks, "So, I'm going to make these first two syrups at the same time, as they follow the same basic procedure. Now, the one on the left, I'm going to call counter culture cola. It's not your average cola recipe. It's pretty underground. You've probably haven't heard of it. And it starts out with six ounces of brown sugar," followed by the sound of something being poured into a container. The speaker continues, "about eight anise pods," as items are dropped into a container. "Two teaspoons of cinnamon and half a teaspoon of nutmeg, both fresh," followed by another dropping sound. "Two tablespoons of grated ginger and two teaspoons of orange zest," accompanied by a dropping sound. "And one cup of orange juice, which I hope came from that orange you just zested," followed by the sound of liquid being poured. A robotic voice says, "On line." The person continues, "And the other syrup we're working with today is basil strawberry syrup. And it contains 12 ounces of honey by weight," followed by a clinking sound and the sound of something viscous being poured. The speaker says, "Sticky little devil." The robotic voice says, "Go for the real stuff that has the name of an actual plant on it. Also, your face is a sticky little devil." The person says, "Half a cup of lemon juice," as liquid is poured. The robotic voice says, "You're just going to ignore that, aren't you?" The person says, "One cup of torn basil," followed by a dropping sound. The robotic voice says, "Oh well." The person concludes, "And about a pound of strawberries, which I killed in the food processor," followed by a plopping sound.
A man speaks, "Heat both of these to a simmer to dissolve the sugar solutions, and then allow to steep for an hour," accompanied by a simmering sound.

A person speaks in a clear, instructional voice, "Strain the syrup, and then add a fourth of a teaspoon of yeast to a 32-ounce bottle, and dilute with freshly squeezed water until there's only a little headroom left." A musical chord plays.

A male speaker says, "So this last soda is the oddball of the group. Someone already rooted out all the puns and beat me to them, so I'm just going to call this one beet soda. Which starts out with one and a half cups of beet juice." A sound of liquid pouring is heard. A deep, distorted voice says, "The red coloring reminds me of your blood." The first speaker continues, "Half a cup of apple juice, which is from Braeburn apples, and half a cup of pomegranate juice," followed by the sound of liquid pouring. He adds, "and one and a half cups of freshly squeezed water," as more liquid is poured. The speaker then says, "Now at this point, you can change the dilution of the soda to fit your taste. If you want to dull the excessive earthiness of this drink, what you should do is take half a cup of this, dilute it to four cups, and then add our five ounces of sugar. But if you like beets, and I mean really like beets, you should add the sugar right now." The sound of an ingredient being poured from a container is heard, and the speaker exclaims, "Like this! And then bring to a simmer to dissolve the sugar."
A man speaks in a clear voice, "fill the bottle and add yeast just like before, replacing any lost water, and this time using a clear bottle to show off that brilliant betalain burst of color."

A person speaks, "So after two days of fermentation at room temperature, you should open your soda to check for carbonation and put it in the fridge to prevent over-fermentation. If you don't, it'll end up like this." A loud pop sounds, followed by laughter. The person speaks again, "Now I hope you could see that soda making is a fun and slightly messy process." Another loud pop is heard. The person continues, "But if you want to make some flavors of your own, keep the sugar relatively constant at 6 ounces for 32 ounces of soda. Who knows, maybe you'll come up with a flavor that really pops. I'm so lonely." This is followed by 8-bit music.

audio_captions: Upbeat, fast-paced electronic music with a chiptune-style melody and synthesized percussion.

A character speaks, "With its factory tuning and data center DNA, an Intel 730 series SSD is an amazing choice for gamers and performance enthusiasts." An electronic chime is heard. Another character speaks, "This isn't my first experience with the Pebble ecosystem, and you can find my original review in the video thumbnail here." A clicking sound is heard. "But, if you don't feel like watching that, I'll summarize for you. The Pebble is one of those few products that changed the way I go about my daily life. The App Store has improved the product further since my original review with easy access to apps for better music control, forcing your phone to ring when you can't find it, and much more stuff like that, and even better. But even though I'm not a heavy app user, 'worth every penny' only begins to describe how I felt about my vanilla Pebble. So for the first time, pretty much ever, I ordered the Pebble Steel the second I heard about it instead of waiting to see if it was good. And here is my review of the unit I bought that ended up being delayed five months because of a shipping address mix-up that to Pebble's credit, they did eventually resolve to my satisfaction. Speaking of things they resolved to my satisfaction, my original Pebble actually started glitching out around the same time my Steel arrived. And while it's disappointing that the screen is displaying gobbledygook a lot of the time, it is actually still somewhat usable and after a couple quick messages to their support, they're shipping me a new one and I don't even appear to have to send the original back. So two thumbs up for saving me the cost of shipping the unit. On to the Steel now." A tapping sound is heard. "I think the packaging actually says just about everything there is to say about this product versus the original." A tapping sound is heard. "It looks great, feels premium," A tapping sound is heard. "and the message that it gets across is, 'Hey, we may still be the same company with the same basic product, but we're all grown up now. Check us out.' And that's what Steel is. Compared to the original Pebble, the main stuff hasn't changed. It has the same sized E Ink display with unchanged contrast and resolution, things I'd like to see upgraded in a future revision. The battery life is the same, the button layout is the same, it's still waterproof, the Bluetooth connectivity is unchanged, and it's still compatible with all the same apps. The improvements are all in the design, which is great because let's face it, Pebble owners, most of the comments we get about our watches sound more like, 'What the heck is that?' versus, 'Oh, wow, that's great. What is it?' And there's a big difference. Now that changes. The Steel is available in..."

A person speaks, "matte black or brushed stainless steel, and both bottles ship with a leather strap pre-attached and a metal wristband that was a touch big for me out of the box but has an included screwdriver and uh the ability to shorten it so I was able to resize it and swap it myself. Pebble doesn't recommend doing this yourself but aside from the pins being extremely tight on mine, I had a pretty hard time with that. I didn't have too much difficulty and this guide here got me through it in about 20 minutes. Now that I've tried both, I think I'm going to stick with the metal band for now. Honestly, they're both great and whichever one you like better is 100% a personal choice. The leather one is lighter, not waterproof and feels a bit more casual, while the steel one feels, aside from the added weight and bulk, uh slightly more comfortable on my wrist with the waterproofness being a nice touch. So there's the pros and cons of each of those. Moving past the strap, the watch face itself has gotten a nice upgrade too. It's smaller overall with cleaner, straighter lines, the bezel is smaller particularly on the top and bottom, the buttons are closer together with a nicer tactile feel to them and the front plastic of the original pebble has been replaced with gorilla glass." A tapping sound is heard. "a welcome upgrade. I mean I may not do hard manual labor every day but I do work with my hands sometimes like even just in computers and I have scratched the bejeebus out of my original pebble. This should hold up much better. The last upgrade is actually a pretty minor one. There's a little RGB LED for charge status indication and app developers I guess can make use of it at some point but I haven't seen any news posted about it in the last few months. Correct me if I'm wrong. So um looks like it hasn't really been used much yet. Which closes out the positive points that I'm going to make in this review and leads well into my one complaint. Pebble."

An exasperated male voice says, "Seriously? You changed the charging cable? It's one thing to have a proprietary charging connector. This is followed by a thumping sound.
A high-pitched voice yells, "Pebble! What the heck?"

A man speaks quickly and clearly, "I really hope this doesn't turn into a trend, and I hope that they've given this iteration a little bit more thought for the future so I don't need to run out and buy new charging cables every time I upgrade my watch to the latest and greatest, as I'm very likely to do. A person speaks, "Well, I like their charging cable, I like that it's magnetic, I like that it's easy to use."

A person speaks, "but I just really wish they wouldn't change it all the time. And I guess that's pretty much it. I loved the Pebble. So you may see a review on that one when the software improves, but for now, Pebble's still my go-to, my experience."

A person speaks in a clear voice: "hasn't been without its rough patches as I outlined at the beginning of this video, but they've managed to make it right every time. A woman speaks, "of the mission. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk says the trip should take about a week to pull off. The two customers will launch on top of the Falcon Heavy. And the passengers will ride inside the crew Dragon capsule, an upgraded version of the Dragon cargo capsule. SpaceX has already been developing the crew Dragon to carry astronauts to and from the station for NASA as part of the commercial crew program. To get back, the Crew Dragon will re-enter Earth's atmosphere and land the passengers, hopefully, gently. A person speaks, "While this is new territory for SpaceX, the moon mission sounds an awful lot like another upcoming space mission, one that NASA wants to do. This is accompanied by a soft, continuous electronic hum.
A woman speaks, "...us into deep space and onto Mars someday. The SLS hasn't..." This is accompanied by the sound of machinery humming.

A female voice speaks, "in late 2018. But recently..."
A woman says, "NASA said it was going to look into maybe putting people on the first flight of the SLS, possibly for a mission in late 2019," all accompanied by background music.

A character speaks, "That trip will take a two-person crew riding inside the Orion crew capsule on an eight or nine-day mission around the Moon and back." A thoughtful "Hmm" is heard, followed by the statement, "That sounds familiar." This is all accompanied by a synthesized musical track.

A female voice speaks, "So, with this moon mission announcement, SpaceX seems to have created a bit of a space race between the public and private sector. The company is sending the message that it can do what NASA plans to do, only faster. It seems like a political move for SpaceX too since the new administration may be more interested in using the private space industry. SpaceX's Falcon Heavy looks to be significantly cheaper than the SLS, so officials may be interested in using the more cost-efficient option to explore space instead of what NASA's building." This is accompanied by subtle electronic beeps and ambient tones.

A female voice speaks clearly, "But there are a few big caveats to consider. First of all, NASA's vehicles have a lot of support in Congress, so they probably won't be replaced by SpaceX anytime soon. Plus, SpaceX is terrible about meeting deadlines. The Falcon Heavy was originally supposed to debut in 2013 or 2014, but its flight has been repeatedly pushed back to this year. There are also some questions of safety." This is all accompanied by light, rhythmic background music.
A woman speaks, "fifty. Within the past two years, two of SpaceX's..."
A person speaks, "nine rockets have exploded. Elon argues that the Falcon 9 is..."
A person speaks, "success rate is still quite high, but that there will definitely be risk involved with the moon mission. He says the customers are entering this with their eyes open."
A person speaks, saying, "Good, 'cause it's gonna be one hell of a view. If the trip is..."

A woman speaks over a futuristic background hum, "successful. Elon sees these private moon vacations as being a big source of revenue for SpaceX. He thinks there's a market for at least one or two trips a year, and the missions could account for 10 to 20% of SpaceX's revenue." A soft electronic swoosh sound plays. She continues, "As for how much each mission will cost, he estimates a little more than the cost of taking people to the International Space Station. Right now, NASA pays between 70 and 80 million to send just one astronaut to the station on a Russian Soyuz rocket. So, if we're operating in that ballpark, I guess I'm going to start saving now." After a sigh, she says, "So Elon clarified that these people aren't from Hollywood. Uh, but Elon announced this moon vacation while I was on vacation. So, I think it's only fair that I become one of the people to go for free," followed by a light chuckle.

audio_captions: Melodic, synthesized music plays.

A man speaks, "Hey guys, back photography here and today we are looking at a portrait session I did with Jasmine Sarah. I'll leave a link to her Instagram in the description if you're interested in seeing more of her work. And if you're new here, please click that subscribe button and hit the notification bell," followed by a notification bell dinging, "so you can keep up with all the latest videos that I put out." A whooshing sound is heard. "So I'm going to leave some raw files from this photo shoot in the description, in the Dropbox link, just in case you want to edit along or just have a play with the files yourself. So, in this video we're going to look at..." This is all accompanied by soft, electronic ambient music.
Soft, melodic music plays as a person says, "this photo in particular, and we're going to look at all the equipment that I used to take this photo."

A person speaks, "go into the camera settings and look at that as well, and then we're going to go into the lighting techniques that we used, and then finally we're going to jump into Photoshop and go through the editing that we did on this photo. So the equipment I used for this photo was a..." The speech is accompanied by background music and punctuated by subtle electronic sounds.
Upbeat electronic music plays as a male voice speaks, "Canon 5D Mark IV with a Sigma 85 1.4 Art lens."

A man speaks in a clear voice, "And there's a link in the description to all of this equipment as well. The settings in the camera were an aperture of F1.4, a shutter speed of 1/1600th of a second, and an ISO of 200. So the reason I use an aperture of F1.4 is to really blow out the background and draw focus to the subject of this photo, which is Jasmine. I shot at a shutter speed of 1/1600th of a second because it was a really bright day outside, so I really had to stop down the shutter speed just so I could get a nice exposure in the image. And I shot at an ISO of 200 because that is the native ISO of the Canon camera I was using, which meant I got the best, clean signal to my sensor, which meant that I could have the most dynamic image possible. So let's talk about lighting for a second. I shot with Jasmine at 3:00, and where we are at the moment, it goes dark about 5:00, and that meant that the sun was really nice and low in the sky. And basically what that means is that there's not going to be any really harsh highlights and shadows. Also, we were really lucky to have clouds in the sky which acted like a really big softbox on our light source. So here are a few more images from the day and then we'll go into Photoshop and start looking at the editing on this image." This is all accompanied by soft, electronic background music.

A man speaks clearly, "Okay, so we're in Camera Raw here, which is a plugin of Photoshop, and we're just going to boost the clarity of the entire image just to make Jasmine pop from the background a little bit more. The next thing we're going to do is just drop the shadows a little bit, add some contrast, and drop the blacks. And basically, the reason for that is because I shot in raw, often the shadows aren't as deep and dense as they could be, just because the raw files are giving you as much flexibility as possible by keeping the contrast low in the image. So the next thing we're going to do is just get the paint brush tool, and I'm just going to mask all of the skin on her face which I want to be smoother. So I'm just dropping the exposure, the shadows, and the blacks just so I can use this brush as a masking tool, just so I can get all of the parts of her skin which I'd want to make smoother later on. And I'm making sure not to go over any contrasting lines that I want to keep sharp, such as her eyebrows, parts of her nose, and lips, and things like that. So now that I've done that, I'm just going to drop the clarity so that her skin smooths out a little bit. And basically, what dropping the clarity does is just smooths out the skin, gets rid of any contrasting lines. Next thing we're doing here is just adding a little bit more clarity and exposure to the eyes, just to make them really pop out of the image. Now, you've got to be really careful with that just because if you go too much, too bright, you can give your model laser beam eyes. So what we're doing here is just adding a little bit more darkness to her lips and her eyebrows. Next step, we're going to drop the exposure, shadows, and blacks again, just so we can use the paint brush as a masking tool to mask all of her hair, so we can make it a little bit brighter in post-production. Okay, now that we've done that, we're going to add some saturation and just change the color balance of her hair very slightly into a more yellow and purple color, just to make her hair look a little bit more orange and stand out a little bit more. Alright, I think that's pretty much everything in Camera Raw. One last thing we'll do is just add a little bit of clarity to her clothing just to make it a little bit more interesting and to pop out a little bit more. Because her whole body was in focus, adding a little bit more clarity to her body just makes it stand out a little bit more. So one final thing we're doing here is just going to make a mask of the entire background. And then once we've done that, we're just going to add a little bit more warmth to the image. Because it wasn't an overcast day, the background is a little bit colder than I like. So we're just going to get a whole mask of the background and make it a little bit more yellow just so the image looks a little bit more warm. Okay, so that's everything in Camera Raw. Now let's jump into native Photoshop and finish off this edit. So the first thing we'll do in Photoshop is just get rid of any blemishes that we can see on her skin. Jasmine's skin was actually really, really good, so there isn't much work to do here, just a little bits and pieces here and there. So, last thing to do is just make Jasmine's hair a little bit more full and thick. Just makes the entire image look a little bit more dramatic, and that's everything. I really hope you liked this video. Please leave a like and subscribe if you did, and remember all of the images from the shoot can be found in the description along with all of the camera equipment used for these photos. So once again, thank you very much for watching, and I'll see you in the next one." This is all accompanied by upbeat electronic music.

audio_captions: A series of cinematic whooshing sounds are followed by a deep, resonant impact. A mechanical click, a low hum, a bright crystalline sound effect, another crisp click, and a low, sustained synthesized tone are then heard in succession.

A female speaker says in an upbeat voice, "Greetings Mobile Delegates. I'm Ashley Esqueda and it's time for your Mobile Nations Monday brief where I bring you the best of the iPhone blog, Crackberry, Android Central, pre-central and Windows Phone Central. It was a busy week this week in mobile, so let's get into it." This is accompanied by a rhythmic, electronic beat.

Electronic music plays. A woman speaks: "Phil over at Android Central put up the definitive review of the Motorola Droid RAZR, the super thin, cut you like a knife phone on Verizon's LTE network. So, what is the verdict? Well, the phone just came out this last Friday."

An energetic female voice speaks, "And Phil says that, well, it's one of the best phones that Verizon's got on its network. It's super fast, dual-core processors, it's beautiful HD display, and its ultra-thinness make for an excellent device for any..." This is accompanied by rhythmic electronic music.

A female speaker says, "any Android user out there. But there are some drawbacks. Yes, that's right. You can't remove the battery on the Razr, which is kind of a bummer especially for the power user out there who likes to swap out batteries midday. And it comes installed with a metric load of bloatware. So that's sort of a bummer. But uh, I'm curious. Have you gone out Android fans and picked up a Motorola Razr or will you be waiting for the Ice Cream Sandwich flagship Galaxy Nexus device on Verizon? Let me know." This speech is accompanied by upbeat electronic music.

A female voice speaks, "Derek and the team over at PreCentral were waiting on bated breath this last week as we heard that Hewlett-Packard was holding an all hands on deck meeting with the webOS team. So what did it mean?" This is accompanied by a rhythmic, electronic beat.
A person speaks, "Meg got up in front of the team and said, 'It's not quite apparent what to do here. I just don't know.'" This is accompanied by rhythmic background music.

A woman speaks: "So, now we're wondering what's going to happen in terms of are they going to keep webOS? Are they going to sell it to the highest bidder or Meg Whitman had some pretty inspiring words at least to Derek where she said that if they were going to commit to webOS, it would be a significant and multi-year commitment that they would be making to the beleaguered operating system. Windows Phone Central had a lot of fun this past week over in New York City because Microsoft held a spend the night party, which was pretty amazing. It was in a huge square with a even huger Windows phone that they built and they did all kinds of crazy stuff in it. And really words can't describe how great it was, so I'm just going to have to show you what happened via the Microsoft video." This is all accompanied by upbeat, electronic background music.
Upbeat electronic music with a driving beat.
Upbeat electronic music plays, featuring a record scratch sound. A male voice asks, "Will you marry me?"
A high-pitched scream.
A female voice laughs and exclaims, "Yes!", followed by the loud cheering of a crowd.
A segment of electronic music with a rhythmic beat.
A female voice speaks, "Favorites of mine include the live-action Fruit Ninja guy and the Plants vs. Zombies people." This is accompanied by upbeat electronic music.

A woman speaks, "The CrackBerry Nation was a little bit disappointed after BlackBerry DevCon because we didn't see any new actual phones running BBX. But Alex Anders over at RIM is reassuring all of you BlackBerry addicts out there with some absolute confirmed specs on the BlackBerry Colt. So this is the code name for the newest BBX flagship device that's going to be coming out hopefully early next year. It's actually going to have HD, the screen is going to be HD, it's going to have the same ratio as the playbook and you're talking about 4.1 inches of screen with 1024x600 resolution, which is insane. So but I'm curious about something in particular for you BlackBerry owners out there and please enlighten me in the comments. I know that BlackBerry is really known for its fantastically designed keyboards and this is one of the things that I hear BlackBerry owners just rave about nonstop. So my question is, is if RIM decides to go forward with touchscreen only BlackBerrys, will you stay?" This is all accompanied by rhythmic electronic background music.

A person speaks, "Over on Tiy, the gang reported on the release of iOS 5.0.1, which is the most recent, brand new, very first update to iOS 5. So, what exactly are we getting in this? We're not seeing a lot of new features like we did when iOS 5 launched, which was a major release, but we are seeing original iPad owners." This is accompanied by upbeat electronic music.

A woman speaks against a backdrop of upbeat electronic music, "getting multi-touch gestures, which is super cool. There are some battery life issues that have been fixed and some other bugs that have allegedly been ironed out. But make sure if you are running a jailbroken iPad, iPhone, iPod touch, that you don't accept this update, whether it's over the air or via USB connection. You definitely want to refrain from updating your jailbroken device. But you already knew that, right? Well, Mobile Nations delegates, that is it for your Monday brief. Be sure to check out all of our podcasts. You can see or hear them at mobilenations.com/shows. Be sure to subscribe to our YouTube channel at youtube.com/mobilenations and you can find me on Twitter at Ashley Esqueda. Nations, you have been briefed." The music concludes with a dramatic stinger.

audio_captions: Two thwacking sounds are followed by a high-pitched, enthusiastic voice shouting, "Excellent!"

A man speaks over the sound of a crowd talking: "Hey guys, welcome back to CES 2017 coverage. I am at Corsair. I'm going to start off talking about what Corsair is most well known for, at least what they started off with, I think, in the PC space, which is memory. What they've done here is taken their Vengeance memory modules that have LEDs in them, like these over here, and they've made them RGB. Because as soon as they gave people the ability to have lights in their memory, people were like, we want those lights to be able to be different colors. So it's a Vengeance RGB RGB series. We're expecting it later this quarter. So it's not quite ready yet, but they've been working on developing the software. So they have Corsair Link, which integrates with that with them."
A person speaks, "You can control each LED individually, you can control them as a group, you can assign".
A man speaks, "in different groups with different profiles to them."
A person speaks, "and then you can go in here and adjust different effects, of course. So you can if change the effect." This is accompanied by the background murmur of other people talking.

Against a backdrop of crowd chatter, a man speaks: "with how quickly the colors change, make it faster or slower. Any of the effects that you might expect when it comes to like breathing and color change and that kind of thing, is already integrated here even though they're still using kind of a beta version of the software. So that's pretty cool. There's a challenge with integrating RGB LEDs because they didn't want to have any external wires or anything like that connected to it. So it's all controlled directly through the DIMM slot or the it's powered through the DIMM slot and communicates with the motherboard through the DIMM slot, but it also has actually the capability to store your profile on the memory module itself. So if you have it installed in a system and configure stuff with the Corsair Link software, you can take the DIMMs out, put them in a put 'em in a different system and they'll keep doing the RGB cycle or whatever profile that you set up. So that's kind of cool. I want to really quickly mention this right here, the Force Series MP500. It's been a while since Corsair came out with a new SSD, so they decided to jump up to the newest and fanciest type of SSD that you can do which is an M.2 SSD with NVMe support. There's not a whole lot to say about it other than that it's got a nice black PCB so it's going to blend in with your build pretty nicely. A bit of yellow accent on the label as far as what they have here. Available in 120, 240, and 480 gig capacities, M.2 2280 form factor and they don't have the read and write speeds listed here, so I don't know what they are, but I think they're pretty good. I believe the reads are well over 2000 and the writes are in the one to 2000 range but don't quote me on that. I'm planning on getting one of these and doing a video on it so I'll bring you more information on that when it's available. Over here we have a new series of power supplies and these are budget series power supplies. They've had the CM series for quite a while. You know, those are the power supplies that are very good and get the job done, but Kyle and I constantly tell constantly tell people to upgrade them when they have them in systems. 'Cause you got to peel off the label 'cause it was kind of a brighter green color and then the cabling itself was not quite as appealing as it could have been. It had ketchup and mustard going on. So, Corsair is replacing that with the TX series right here. They have a 550, 650, 750, and 850 watt versions. They're partially modular but the cables as you can maybe see here are all black. So budget power supply, Corsair quality, no hideous colors that might mismatch with your build and and get yeah, get a new power supply. Also, the HX series has been updated. Remove, basically they've removed the the I from it. It's just the HX whatever, not like the 1200i like they have over there. They gutted the Corsair Link capabilities from these power supplies. So they're more straightforward power supplies, but by doing that they can reduce the price by they'd said about $20 per unit. And finally we have the product that I think Corsair was most excited about which is the newest..."
A person says, "version of their K95 keyboard, which is called the K95 RGB Platinum."
A male voice speaks, "'cause everything that's platinum is usually the best that's possible. But basically the way Corsair has updated the uh..."
A man speaks, "previous K95s is they've added a light bar across the top. It's got 18..."
A male voice speaks, "18 different LED illumination areas and uh they're all very smooth, so you can't really tell where the LEDs are, so..."

A person speaks, "as it's doing a nice effect across there. You don't like to see, oh, there's an LED and there's an LED. It's just sort of a nice fluid motion. Of course, you're going to have the Corsair software available for these, which is insanely powerful and what you can do is when it comes to configurations and stuff. And they have community members who have dropped in profiles that you can load up and that kind of thing, which is really cool."
A male voice speaks, "They've taken the G keys over here, the macro keys, and they've narrowed it down to just a single row, which is a little bit simpler."

A person speaks, "and those do have texture on them, so you can feel if you're touching those or touching the keys next to them. This one is using Cherry MX speed switches, which Corsair recently launched just this past year, and I believe they're going to have them in other varieties as well. But, you know, the speed switches are unique to Corsair right now from Cherry, so they're they're trying to push those as much as possible. It's got the features that you already had and still want, like your media controls on the top right. And it's got a nice feature for the rest wrist rest, which is this little magnetic piece right here." All of this is accompanied by indistinct background chatter.

A person speaks, "So if you like a little bit more texture, you can flip it to one side. If you like a little bit more smooth, flip it to the other." A magnetic clicking sound is heard, and the person continues, "and a magnet just holds it in place. So you can easily change your wrist rest up."

A person speaks, "The final thing is it's got 8 megabytes of internal memory. So of course any of the profiles that you save, you can save internally. Uh, even if they're more complex ones like RGB profiles. And then you have three internal profiles that you can switch between using that button." This is accompanied by background chatter.
A person speaks, "on the top left. So you don't need the Corsair software installed if".

A man speaks amidst background chatter and crowd noise, saying, "take this uh keyboard and use it on a different computer or something like that. This keyboard is supposed to come out in Q1, I believe that means should be in the next".
A person speaks, "month or two and I'm supposed to get one and do a review on it. So you should be seeing a little bit more coverage on this in the near future."
A man speaks in a clear voice, "But that's all we have here from the Corsair suite except one last thing I wanted to show you." This is accompanied by clicking sounds.
A person speaks, saying, "which is just some shots of this pink system that they built which is Diva themed which made me think I needed..."
A male voice says, "steal it and give it to my wife, cause she really likes to play D.Va."
A person says, "really cool build. I mean, you don't see pink builds too often. It's water-cooled inside, everything." This is accompanied by background chatter.

audio_captions: The sound of a drum beating rhythmically is followed by a man speaking, "I think probably every nation on Earth has at one point claimed to have discovered America. For instance, there's theories that the Chinese did, 9th century Arabs did, the Zeno brothers from Venice did, and 14th...". This is accompanied by the sound of birds chirping.

Birds chirp as a man with a calm, clear voice speaks, "century Molly, but I'm going to give you another possible theory, the Welsh. The story goes that when Owen Gwynedd died in 1170, his sons began to fight for power and one of his sons..."

A man speaks, "was angered by this so decided to set sail with a hundred men and he formed a colony in America. The earliest sources of this story, however, only appear in the late 15th century." Birds are chirping in the background.

A person speaks, "after Columbus discovered America, but this story could well have changed the entire political landscape of the new world. It's because Spain and Portugal have". This is accompanied by faint background music.

A person speaks, "largely divided the new world between themselves with Portugal taking Brazil, Africa, and Asia, and Spain taking the rest of the new world. However, this myth could have given the English a claim." This is accompanied by a low, ambient musical score.

A man speaks, "to the Americas and early imperialists like John D often made references to it. None of the proponents of this myth could ever agree as to where Madoc would have landed," accompanied by the sound of birds chirping.

A character speaks, "Mexico, Newfoundland, or Alabama. But when the Virginia colony was established, they quickly went to work trying to find his descendants, the Welsh Indians. Almost straight away, William Newport said the Monacan Indians were the Welsh Indians."
A male voice speaks, "caste sounded somewhat Welsh, and it was a great relief that they were so close to England." This is accompanied by gentle background music.

A person speaks, "the only colony at the time, but as England expanded, so too did the claims. For instance, William Penn's deputy said it was the dog Indians and he said that he also preached the Bible to them in Welsh. And in the 19th century, the American painter George Catlin said it was". This is accompanied by the sound of birds chirping.
A man speaks, "the Mandan Indians in North Dakota. A Welsh explorer John Evans helped map out the Missouri River in 1804 on his quest to find them." This is accompanied by background music.

A male voice speaks, "and Jefferson also mentions his expeditions in a letter to Lewis and Clark. So some speculate that Jefferson even believed in the existence of Welsh Indians. However, this seems like a bit of a push." This is accompanied by instrumental string music.

audio_captions: Acoustic guitar music plays as a person says, "we take care of the land. We are told it will take care of us."

A person speaks, "We've been here continuously for over 4,000 years. We take great pride in taking care of our our properties. It's something that we can't do alone either." A second person then speaks, "James Kinter is the tribal secretary for the Yocha Dehe Wintun Nation. He works closely with Jim Eters, who oversees all their agricultural operations." Gentle, melodic music plays in the background.

A man speaks, "...as well as building their Seka Hills brand." Another man says, "They really wanted a brand name that connected their Putwin language and the land. And Seka is Putwin for blue, and the blue hills lie along the west side of the Kape Valley." The first man continues, "The tribe farms over 10,000 acres of land in the heart of the valley, with 124 of those acres devoted to growing olives." The second man adds, "Western Yolo County really has the ideal Mediterranean climate and the heat we get here in the Kape Valley during the summer produces really big flavors." A third man says, "We felt that it was a crop that was uh good for the environment out here. It's good for the soil. It's drought tolerant as well, unlike nut trees that were uh in the area before." The first speaker says, "Like the Corasi family, a majority..." This is all accompanied by gentle acoustic guitar music.
A person speaks, "many of their trees are planted extremely close together."
A male voice states, "what they and others call super high density planting," while gentle, melodic music plays.
A man speaks, "and it takes a certain type of olive to not only handle the compact conditions, but be able to produce a quality oil."

A person says, "So these are Arbequina olives and it's a very small olive, uh, not what you typically see for table olives. It's a lot of pit, but within the flesh, uh, is quite a bit of oil. The reason it's such a popular olive for..." This is accompanied by a faint rustling sound.

A person speaks, saying, "oil is because it has a high oil content." Another person then speaks in a clear voice, saying, "Arbequina olives are the major players, but there's a variety of olive called the".
A man speaks, "Qual, making its debut at Seca Hills."

A man speaks, "unlike the Arbaquina, the Piqual is grown in a more traditional style of planting, otherwise known as medium density." A second man then says, "We're excited to harvest some of that for the first time this fall and are working on other varietals that offer the full spectrum of flavor from the very mild oils all the way to the very robust and pungent oils. We really wanted to provide a full-service facility. We wanted to be able to process the olives, store the oil, and bottle it." The sound of machinery running can be heard.

A man speaks, "...in one location. And not only do we do that for our own fruit, but we also offer those services to other local growers." This is followed by instrumental guitar music. Another man says, "Not only has the Tribal Council opened their doors to nearby growers, but also to the public." The first man continues, "We opened the Se Hill's tasting room and we continue to see more and more traffic. It's really a key to educating consumers is to get that oil in front of them and have them taste it." He later adds, "I think as the consumer becomes more educated, they're going to seek out different varietals. They're going to uh taste those for different flavor profiles."

A man speaks, "just like you would with wine. We're proud of this land, we try to take care of it. We want to make sure that we're taking care of it for the future for our people and for our neighbors too." Another man says, "Being able to work with the council to develop it from the ground floor has been awesome and there's been a lot of challenges along the way. Of course, it's farming, but I think that we're to a point now where things are looking pretty good. There's nowhere to go but up." All of this is accompanied by acoustic guitar music.

Today, however, that fascination may be stronger than ever before. From Star Wars to Japanese anime, elements of samurai culture are everywhere to be seen." This is accompanied by light music from a stringed instrument.
A man says, "a little wonder because Japanese armor is of brilliant design," accompanied by gentle music.
A bell chimes, and a man speaks, "a perfect balance of form and function, majesty and psychological intimidation." This is followed by another chime.
A man speaks, "Japanese armor as we know it, developed over a long period," accompanied by gentle, traditional-sounding music.
A man speaks, "Up until the 14th or 15th century, battles in Japan were mostly contained skirmishes between rival clans." This is accompanied by subtle instrumental music.
A male voice speaks in a clear, measured tone, "After the 15th century, generals participated in all-out warfare."
A man speaks, "pitting hundreds and sometimes thousands of soldiers against each other in one battle." Faint background music plays, and a page-turning sound effect is heard.

A man speaks in a clear voice, "An elaborate costume or helmet would make them easily recognizable," accompanied by a low, ambient drone.
A man speaks in a clear voice, "By the 16th century, fanciful elaborate helmets began to make their appearance. These were known as Kawari Kabuto or strange helmets."

A man speaks in a clear voice, "composed of lacquer, wood, and paper over a simple metal bowl, they allowed for extremely fancy..." This is accompanied by a gentle, melodic tune played on a string instrument.
A male voice speaks, "creations, sometimes reaching up to 2 feet high." This is accompanied by gentle background music.
A male voice speaks, "16th-century armorers' catalogs tell of wild creations ordered by their samurai patrons." This is accompanied by light background music.

A man speaks in a clear, narrative voice, "This helmet is is adorned with a gold lacquer maedate or fore-crest."
A male speaker says, "fitted with tufts of hair, this demon makes a very strong impression at first sight," accompanied by gentle, traditional-sounding instrumental music.

audio_captions: A man speaks in a clear, conversational tone, "Right guys, welcome down to this week's Tech Tuesday, which is not on a Tuesday, but with the way the videos have worked this week, it wasn't possible to get it out, but there is a lot of stuff to be chatting about this week. So first things first, Callaway have launched some new irons." This is followed by the sound of a golf club head tapping lightly.
A man speaks clearly, "The Kirkland Signature ball is back on the shelves."

A person speaks in a clear, moderate voice, "and the way that golfers are buying their equipment is starting to change. So first up, Callaway have brought out two new irons. Now, these particular ranges, they've been dormant for a number of years now. So it's the Apex MB and the X Forged. Now, out of these two irons, the Apex MB looks unbelievably sexy. It is a shiny, small, thin top line, pure blade. And out of the two that have been brought out, that's probably the most pretty. It is just a gorgeous, gorgeous looking iron. Now, as you look at this iron, you may realize that it is very much aimed at the tour pro slash the very, very good amateur. And Callaway have really come out and said that they're not catering towards a higher handicapper with this iron. This is unashamedly based at the better player. And you can really see by looking at it, you are not going to get any forgiveness if you hit this iron slightly bad."

A man speaks: "Now, for many people, they won't be actually interested in buying these irons. For a start, they are very, very top-end as far as price is concerned. But the X-Forged iron, that is something that a lot more people will be interested in."

A person speaks, "So unusually for Callaway, the X-Forged series are actually quite staggered in the amount that they're released. So there's a set came out 2007, then 2009, and then 2013. There's a great picture here from GolfWRX which shows the last two incarnations, so the 2013 version, and now the 2017 version side by side."

A man speaks clearly, "So the X Forged is still a better player's iron, but it does offer a little bit more forgiveness. It is slightly bigger. Both these irons are forged. Both of them look amazing. But please comment below which one would you be more interested in trying. I know the X Forged iron was very, very popular when it came out."
A man speaks, saying, "and I know a lot of people will be very interested in getting their hands on this and trying them out."

A man with a clear voice speaks, "In other golf club news, Fried Eggs Golf, who I'm a big fan of their channel, released a brilliant, brilliant skit about the new TaylorMade irons with the speed foam. I'm going to include a link in the description. So please, please go check it out. It is absolutely awesome."

A person speaks, "Now exciting news for anyone who managed to get their hands on the Costco ball, the Kirkland Signature last year. It is back. Now this golf ball caused an absolutely massive buzz earlier this year. It is a four-piece tour performance golf ball that when many people were testing said performed just as well as the Pro V1, as the TP5, as the top balls out there for a fraction of the cost. So this ball is available for $29.99 and it has just come back and hit the shelves."
A man speaks in a clear voice, "Now remains to be seen if this is exactly the same Kirkland signature ball after a little bit of research and a few people contact."

A man speaks, saying, "me, the Kirkland Signature ball from earlier this year and last year was manufactured as far as I'm aware by a company called Nassau. And I had some Nassau Quattro balls, so a four-piece tour performance ball delivered to me and really did enjoy that performance. If it is the same ball, if it's been manufactured by Nassau again, then it's going to be a cracker, but I don't know if it is exactly the same, but it is good news for anyone who enjoyed using this ball that it is back and as certainly last time they absolutely flew off the shelves. So if Costco are going to go big guns on this, if they're going to try and incur the wrath, well not try and incur, incur the wrath of the big manufacturers like Titleist who tried to sue them over patent infringements on this ball, we will wait to see, but did you try this ball out? Comment below, let me know. In other big equipment news, Phil Mickelson has re-signed for Callaway and he has signed a deal that will keep him there until he stops playing professional golf. Now for Callaway, this is quite a big deal. Certainly Phil Mickelson is still a very, very big deal for most golf fans who just love the way he plays. There's no real details of the deal, but all we know is he's going to stay with them until he stops playing professionally. For Callaway it's good, certainly after you see someone like Sergio leave TaylorMade after such a long stint with them. This is probably a good bit of stable news for that company. Also in massive club news, we all know by now that Tiger has been cleared to come back and play. There are no details on when he's actually going to get back to competitive golf, but videos of him actually playing some rounds have hit the web and as always went absolutely mental. And I am excited. I am a Tiger fan. I still think that the game needs him." This is all accompanied by the intermittent sound of a golf club hitting a ball.

A character speaks, "certainly no one who can just engage an audience like he does. If you just wait and see when he does make that competitive return, which hopefully he will do, the TV ratings, the interest in that tournament will absolutely skyrocket. I can't imagine him playing an event before the new year, and I imagine he's going to get himself geared up and ready to play at the Masters. The last videos to come out was when he was at a clinic and someone got a snap of his irons."
A man's voice says, "Now you can see here is a classic blade shape. It's got his TGR initials on there with his logo."

A man speaks, "but they don't look very TaylorMade. So obviously Tiger signed with TaylorMade in January to much fanfare. But these irons do not look like anything TaylorMade have produced. A few people have."
A male voice says, "said this, and it does appear that they were made by Nike according to an inside source."

A person speaks, "So the source that was quoted on GolfWRX used to work at the oven, and he says those TGR blades are sweet. Our source told us, told GolfWRX. Yes, I do know what they are. We made them for him before we were done at Nike. They are special, Nike. They are special and it was a tough project emotionally to give them the focus and passion that we always had, while wondering if these were the last we might ever make for him ever. Now, obviously we don't know the details of Tiger's club deal, but as far as I was aware, it was all throughout the bag. So, it's interesting to see him rocking some blades which potentially were not made by Taylormade. If they are still going to be in his bag when he returns to competitive golf, we will have to wait and see."
A male speaker says, "see. But what do you think of how they look? And are you excited about the potential of Tiger coming back? I am, because I certainly grew up in the Tiger era, but..."
A man speaks, "a lot of people watching this will not have seen him at his best. So by all means comment below, let me know what you think."

A man speaks in a clear voice, "So what we're going to talk about here is a story that actually slipped through my net last month and it is about how golfers' buying habits are changing," accompanied by subtle background music.

A person speaks: "So I'm going to read from an article here from Golf Digest just so I don't get anything wrong here. But Golf Datatech Golf product attitudes and usage study, which is probably why I didn't pay attention to it, probably slipped right through my net with that title. Um, is a demographic portrait of US Golf consumers. But this probably is a trend that we see throughout the world and certainly how it's moving forwards. Um, studied a thousand serious golfers and showed that while golfers often are spending more time holding on to their clubs and deliberating over a purchase for several months, there's been a dramatic change in the role that e-commerce is playing. So what the study is showing is that year on year, golfers are buying more gear online. It's up 50%. Now for green grass retailers, this is actually a pretty big deal. So if more people are heading online to buy clubs, not only clothing but clubs and other hardware as well, that is going to be hitting those retailers in the pocket. Now, some of those retailers are online as well, but a lot of the club pros out there are not. The time that people actually spend between buying clubs, that's staying pretty static, so it's about four years for a driver and similar times for irons, well a little bit longer for irons and putters and wedges and all the rest of it. But the amount that is being spent online now is going to be of a concern to a lot of people unless they start to diversify. But in that marketplace, there's a lot of people who are more established. And is this something that you have seen? Are you spending more of your money online when you're buying golf equipment, especially with clubs, which is a slight concern to me because I always try and recommend people to go get fitted rather than buying online. However, that doesn't seem to be the trend here."

A male voice speaks, "So guys, thank you so much for watching this Tech Tuesday. Make sure you comment below and let me know what you think about all these pieces of news which have been coming out. Please subscribe to the channel if you haven't already. Follow me on my other social media platforms as well. And we will see you down here next time." This is followed by a short musical flourish.

audio_captions: The crack of a baseball bat is heard, followed by a man speaking in an announcer's voice: "What's happening, Big 12 fans? Mitch Gerber from the Big 12 Digital Network bringing you the Big 12 First Pitch Pre-game Show, brought to you by Tire Pros. Let's set the stage for game three here on this beautiful Wednesday afternoon here in Oklahoma City. It's going to be TCU taking on the Baylor Bears, as these two teams met earlier this month, and it was the Bears who took two of three from the Horn Frogs. TCU, however, currently rides a five-game winning streak and completed their..." This is accompanied by background music and crowd chatter.

A man speaks, "sweep of the season this past weekend over Kansas State. For more on TCU, let's head down to Big 12 correspondent, Annabelle Stefan." Upbeat electronic music plays. A woman says, "Thanks, Mitch. Coach, you guys coming out here facing Baylor, what is the mentality of your team right now?" A man replies, "Well, you know, we're excited to be here, excited to play and and specifically, you know, Baylor beat us up pretty good uh two week two weeks ago. So, um, you know, we're excited to have the opportunity to play them again and you know, they have a club that's playing really, really good baseball, as good as as along with West Virginia, probably as good a baseball as being played in this conference. So, uh, I'm sure it'll be a lot of fun." The woman asks, "You mentioned that that last meetup, how do you feel like your team has improved even though it was a short..."

A man speaks, "Uh, you know, I mean, again, it's a short amount of time, you know, I, you know, we've we've gotten better in some areas, but you know, this time of year is gonna be about, you know, how how you perform on the baseball field. And and uh it's not a whole lot of tinkering of lineups, it's just uh, you know, mono y mono, you know, matching up and um whoever plays the best, it's not you know, this this tournament's not going to be about the best team, it's about the team that plays the best. And if we play the best, we'll be around for a while. If we don't, we won't." A woman replies, "Well, good luck out there. Thanks, Coach. Back to you, Mitch." Another man says, "Thanks, Annabelle. Baylor comes into this year's championship just one of two big 12 teams to make it to the tournament every single year in the league's 20-year history. They'll look to ride that momentum here today against a tough TCU team. Let's head down to Christine Williamson with more on the Gritty Bears." Another woman says, "All right, thanks, Mitch. Coach, we're going into this game. It's kind of like a a clean slate going into this um championship. What has been your mindset going into this championship?" A man responds, "You know, the biggest thing is our guys have scratched and crawled to to get into this championship with our past couple weekends that we've played and uh I'm I'm pretty excited about how they are playing. So the biggest thing is we have to play our best baseball in this tournament to get into postseason and uh we have to treat this like it is our..."

A man speaks, "post season. So, uh I'm excited about how we're playing and excited to see how this tournament's going to go." A woman then asks, "And so taking off of that momentum, what has been one of the main things that you've been telling your guys going into this week?" The man replies, "Stay healthy and uh just relax because you know..."
A man speaks, saying, "they've done so much hard work uh to get to this point. I don't want to change what they're doing, but at the same time I I want them to be excited about where they're..."
A person speaks, saying, "are and what they're doing and uh the hard work that they put into it to get to this point. So, uh take advantage of."

A man says, "this second life that we have in regards to getting into a regional and take advantage of it." A woman asks, "What do you think was is one of the biggest challenges going into this week for you guys?" The man replies, "You know, Beanie, I think the biggest thing for us is really just making sure our guys understand the the value and the to really appreciate the experience they're getting. We have some phenomenal teams here in regards to this big 12 tournament. So the way I look at it is as long as we can play well and and take advantage of some mistakes and hopefully not make as many mistakes on our side, we're going to be okay." The woman says, "Awesome. Well, good luck to you," and the man responds, "Thank you very much." The woman then says, "Thanks, Mitch, back to you." Upbeat, rhythmic music plays, followed by another man's voice stating, "Here's a look at today's Tire Pros projected starters. For TCU, it'll be left-handed pitcher Dalen Horton, while Baylor sends left-hander Daniel Castano to the bump. TCU's Horton is 8-0 this season with a 2.35 ERA in 57 and a third innings pitched. TCU is 10 and 1 in games this season that he has started. Castano has a 4 and 4 record with a 4.10 ERA in 83 and a third innings pitched. A trip to play Thursday night is on the line. Bears, Horned Frogs, next right here in Oklahoma City for the Big 12 Digital Network. I'm Mitch Gerber."

A man speaks, saying, "and Serbia. But in this video, I'm talking about Serbia versus Switzerland." This is accompanied by the sound of birds chirping.
A person says, "But before I get into the nitty-gritty of Serbia versus Switzerland, let's recap what has happened so far in Group E." This is accompanied by background music.

A man speaks as birds chirp in the background. "In the opening match of Group E, Brazil and Switzerland played each other to a 1-1 draw. What a big result for Switzerland. That's like a win versus Brazil, a team who has been at every single World Cup tournament dating all the way back to 1930. Like that's a big result, Switzerland. Big, big result. Pat yourself on the back. In that match, the goal scorers were Philippe Coutinho and Steven Zuber from Switzerland. In the second match of the group, Costa Rica played Serbia. This match ended in a 1-0 victory for Serbia, courtesy of a beautiful free kick by the captain and talisman Aleksandar Kolarov. So after those first two fixtures, Serbia sit on top of the group with three points, Brazil second one point, Switzerland third with one point, and Costa Rica at the bottom with zero points. What were my actual Group E predictions for the 2018 World Cup? Well, of course, I'm actually predicting Brazil to top the group, Serbia to come in second, Switzerland to come in third, and Costa Rica to come in last. But right now it seems like it might go a little different. Serbia, they're looking good. Brazil, you know, was slipped up by Switzerland and Costa Rica, it doesn't seem as if they're going to repeat what they did at the 2014 World Cup. But even with that being said, Group E is still quite wide open. So guys, now for a brief World Cup profile for Serbia and Switzerland. For Serbia, they're also known as Orlovi or the Eagles, and this will be their second World Cup appearance as the nation of Serbia. They are the successor team to Yugoslavia and the various name changes that the Yugoslavian nation went through. And they're also the successor team to Serbia and Montenegro. But I really don't want to focus on all those successor team stuff and all of that. I want to focus on the nation of Serbia." A faint siren wails in the distance.

A male voice speaks, "What's the best World Cup finish for the nation of Serbia? Well, they have only qualified once as Serbia and that was at the 2010 World Cup when they made an early group stage exit. That was also the last time they played at the FIFA World Cup."

A person speaks: "For Switzerland, they're also known as the Rosso Crociati or the Red Crosses, and this would be their 11th World Cup appearance. Switzerland also hosted the World Cup in 1954 where they achieved one of their best World Cup finishes, making it to the quarterfinals. Their last World Cup appearance came in 2014 when they made it to the round of 16. Head-to-head, how many times have Serbia and Switzerland faced each other in the past? Zero. This would be the first meeting between these two European teams. As for form at the 2018 World Cup, well for Serbia, they achieved a one-nil win versus Costa Rica in their first game, and I must say that the head coach Krstajić has Serbia looking really, really good."

Birds are chirping in the background as a person speaks: "As for Switzerland, they achieved a 1-1 draw versus Brazil. Like, that's a big team and to get a 1-1 draw, to get a point from them, that's a really, really good achievement. They targeted Neymar and they negated his influence on the game. Switzerland looks a really gritty team under Vladimir Petkovic. What are the players to watch in this match? Well, for Serbia, Aleksandar Kolarov, their left back, their captain, their talisman, their dead ball specialist, scorer in the first game, enough said."
A character speaks, "Another player to watch is Sergej Milinković-Savić. I spoke about him in the last preview that I did and wow, I'm impressed. Now I understand why the big teams want him."

A man speaks in a clear voice: "He had such a great game versus Costa Rica, and I'm looking for him to sizzle again versus Switzerland. Dusan Tadic and Adem Ljajic, they were lively, so look out for those players again. And Luka Milivojevic and Nemanja Matic was solid in midfield. Those are also two more players to watch from Serbia. I'm not too familiar with the Serbian bench, so when the substitutions are made, I will be definitely paying close attention to those players."

A man speaks, "As for Switzerland, Shaqiri was really, really good versus Brazil, and he will need to put in another big performance versus Serbia if Switzerland is to get a favorable result in this game. Maybe a draw. Maybe they can squeeze a draw or even a win, who knows. Also, another player to watch is the goal scorer from the Brazilian match, Steven Zuber."

A male voice speaks clearly, "He was able to muscle off the big Brazilian defender Miranda to score his goal. So that means that Zuber is definitely ready for that physical battle versus Serbia. Also guys, we have to keep our eye on Granit Xhaka and Behrami doing the dirty work deep in the Swiss midfield. These two players will be key versus Matić and Milivojević."

A person speaks, "Also their goalkeeper Yann Sommer, he pulled off a few big saves versus Brazil and he will need to do so again versus Serbia if Switzerland are to stay alive at the 2018 World Cup." This is all accompanied by background music.

A man speaks, "What changes should the head coaches make coming into this fixture? Well, for Serbia, I don't expect them to make any changes unless someone has a niggle or they're not fully fit. But we could also see Krstajić trying Prijović instead of Mitrović, who was a little off his game. You know, Mitrović has been really, really good this season for Fulham, but I don't I don't I don't rate him that highly though. So I would like to see someone else get a look in just so we could know about the options that Serbia has if they ought to make a deep run in the tournament. Or if Mitrović features, he would just have to come good in the match. But I really don't expect Krstajić to make many changes. Maybe one or two the most, but I don't really expect much change to happen to the Serbian 11." This is accompanied by the sound of birds chirping.

A man speaks: "For Switzerland, I'm going to take out Haris Seferović up top and I'm going to bring in either Josip Drmić or Breel Embolo. But unless there's an injury, I don't think that Vladimir Petković is going to really really change up an eleven which scraped a draw versus a team like Brazil. So guys, now for the sweetest part, my prediction. Well, it's not easy coming up with these predictions, guys. You know, I have to think about, you know, how the teams have been playing, you know, who they got result versus, who they lost to, who they won, you know, so it's like, how, how am I going to predict this match? Serbia looks good. Switzerland, they scraped a draw versus Brazil, like Brazil, remember that? So, who am I going to predict to win this match? I have to make a call. You know, it would be nice to play it safe and say a draw, you know, like, oh, I'm going to just play it safe and say a draw. Like I can't go wrong with a draw. Like nobody will get mad at me if I say the match would draw. But I have a I have a feeling that Serbia will do something big in this World Cup. So I'm going to go for Serbia, two goals, Switzerland, one. Serbia will move on to the round of 16 with this win, I think, or they would put themselves in a really, really good position to do so. So I'm going for a 2-1 win for Serbia. What's your predictions? Let me know in the comments section down below. So guys, now for question of the day, question of the day." This is accompanied by the chirping of insects. The speaker slaps a surface twice at the end of the speech.

A person speaks, "I never expected them to do so well at all. Like Ivan Rakitic, Luka Modric has been really, really good. Mario Mandzukic has been annoying as ever and that's how he plays."

A male voice says, "proud of our guys. It's uh, you know, this is what we needed. We've had four horrible weeks. Um, not that we weren't running good, we just got wrecked and unfortunate deals. A man speaks, "Well, what you say? We ran out of gas, it was wrong. I mean, I mean, we were 10 laps to the good. I mean, like I said, it just caught us off guard. A man speaks, "use the term, we're going out to lunch maybe tomorrow to discuss some things and they wanted to make some lunch plans. A man says, "when I got up in the crap and then I just returned the favor a little bit coming to the start finish line. It's Bristol, you know? A second man speaks, "In four of the last five races, Joey Coulter with top 11 finishes, he's now 10th in points."

A person speaks, "Yeah, we did. Unfortunately, just kind of lost a handle on it a little bit.
